definition: to start a new account with a bank
example: Newcomers can open an account with just a passport and their PR card.

definition: a bank account used for everyday payments and spending
vi: tài khoản thanh toán (tài khoản chi tiêu hằng ngày)
example: My pay goes into my chequing account, and I transfer some to savings each month.

definition: a bank account that pays interest on money you keep there
example: A high-interest savings account is a safe place for your emergency fund.
collocations: put money in a savings account

definition: to take money out of a bank account
example: You can withdraw cash from any of our ATMs without paying a fee.

definition: to put money into a bank account
example: You can make a deposit by taking a photo of the cheque in the banking app.
collocations: make a deposit at the ATM

definition: a quick way to send money to someone by email or phone in Canada
example: My roommate sends me his share of the rent by e-transfer on the first of every month.

definition: money a bank charges each time you make a payment or withdrawal
example: Using another bank's ATM usually means paying an extra transaction fee.

definition: when you spend more money than is in your account, borrowing from the bank
vi: tình trạng thấu chi (rút/chi quá số dư tài khoản)
example: I was charged a fee because the payment put my account into overdraft.

definition: a number that shows how reliable you are at paying back money
example: Paying your bills on time is the best way to build a good credit score in Canada.

definition: the maximum amount you can spend on a credit card
example: The bank raised my credit limit after I'd had the card for a year.

definition: the percentage charged for borrowing money or paid for saving it
example: The Bank of Canada lowered its interest rate, which made mortgages slightly cheaper.

definition: a loan from a bank used to buy a home
vi: khoản vay thế chấp mua nhà
example: Our mortgage payments went up by $400 a month when we renewed at a higher rate.

definition: to formally ask a bank to lend you money
example: To apply for a loan, you'll need your recent pay stubs and two pieces of ID.
collocations: apply for a small business loan

definition: to finish paying all of a debt
example: Once we pay off our car loan, we will have more money for travel.
collocations: pay off the balance in full

definition: to owe money to someone
example: Many students can expect to be in debt for years after graduation.
collocations: be in debt to the bank

definition: to spend only the amount of money you planned
vi: chi tiêu đúng theo ngân sách đã định
example: If you stick to a budget, you can save for a vacation without using credit cards.
collocations: find it hard to stick to a budget
set a budget and stick to it

definition: to keep money over time in order to buy something
example: We rarely eat out because we want to save up for a down payment.

definition: to have enough money to pay for something
vi: có đủ khả năng chi trả
example: Many young families can no longer afford a detached house in Vancouver.

definition: money spent on something
example: I track all my monthly expenses in a spreadsheet, from groceries to car insurance.

definition: a document that lists goods or services provided and how much must be paid
example: Please pay the invoice within 30 days of receiving it.

definition: the amount of money currently in a bank account
example: I check my account balance on the app before making large purchases.

definition: a record from the bank listing all money in and out of an account
example: The landlord asked for three months of bank statements to prove my income.

definition: a payment from your account that you did not approve
vi: giao dịch trái phép, giao dịch không được phép
example: I called the bank immediately when I noticed an unauthorized transaction on my credit card.

definition: a payment made electronically straight into someone's bank account
vi: chuyển khoản trực tiếp vào tài khoản (lương, trợ cấp)
example: Set up direct deposit so your tax refund arrives faster.

definition: a professional who helps people plan how to save and invest money
example: Our financial advisor suggested we put more into our RRSPs before the contribution deadline.

definition: money put aside to live on after you stop working
example: Many Canadians worry that their retirement savings won't be enough.

definition: a payment made after the due date
example: A late payment can hurt your credit score and add interest charges.

definition: the smallest amount you must pay on a credit card bill each month
example: If you only make the minimum payment, it can take years to clear your balance.
collocations: pay more than the minimum payment

definition: a regular payment taken automatically from your account with your permission
vi: thanh toán tự động đã được ủy quyền trước
example: I pay my hydro bill through a pre-authorized payment, so I never miss a due date.

definition: the amount of money needed to pay for basic things like housing and food
example: The high cost of living in Metro Vancouver is pushing some families to move to Alberta.

definition: a bank employee who serves customers at the counter
example: The bank teller helped me order a new chequebook and update my address.

definition: a secret number you enter to use a bank card
vi: mã PIN (mã số bí mật của thẻ)
example: Never share your PIN with anyone, even someone who calls and says they work for your bank.

definition: to pay by holding a card or phone near a payment machine
vi: thanh toán chạm (thanh toán không tiếp xúc)
example: Most coffee shops in Vancouver let you tap to pay with your phone.
collocations: tap to pay with a card
tap to pay with your phone

definition: a bank card that takes money directly from your account when you pay
vi: thẻ ghi nợ (trừ tiền trực tiếp từ tài khoản)
example: I use my debit card for groceries so I don't spend money I don't have.

definition: managing your bank account on a website or app
example: With online banking, I can pay my hydro bill without leaving home.

definition: an amount of money charged every month for a service
example: The bank waives the monthly fee if you keep a minimum balance in the account.

definition: a bank account shared by two or more people
vi: tài khoản chung (đứng tên nhiều người)
example: My husband and I opened a joint account to pay our rent and utilities.

definition: one of the local offices of a bank
example: The bank branch near my workplace is closing, so I'll have to go downtown.

definition: to tell your bank that your card is missing so it can be blocked
example: I called right away to report my lost card after I left my wallet on the SkyTrain.
collocations: report a lost or stolen card
call to report a lost card

definition: to move money from one account to another
example: You can transfer funds between your chequing and savings accounts in the app.

definition: not enough money in an account to pay for something
vi: không đủ tiền trong tài khoản
example: My rent payment was returned because of insufficient funds in my account.

definition: to have a cheque refused by the bank because there is not enough money
vi: bị trả lại séc (vì không đủ tiền)
example: My tenant's cheque bounced, so I asked him to send an e-transfer instead.

definition: a cheque with VOID written across it, given to someone so they can see your bank account details
vi: séc đã huỷ (ghi chữ VOID, dùng để cung cấp số tài khoản ngân hàng)
example: My new employer asked for a void cheque to set up direct deposit.

definition: an agreement that lets you borrow money up to a set amount when you need it
vi: hạn mức tín dụng (vay khi cần, trong một mức cho phép)
example: We used our line of credit to cover the unexpected roof repairs.
collocations: apply for a line of credit
draw on a line of credit

definition: the amount of money you still owe
example: Please pay the outstanding balance on your account by the end of the month.

definition: money you must pay for borrowing, especially on a credit card
example: If you pay your full balance every month, you won't have any interest charges.

definition: the usual ways in which a person spends money
example: Tracking every purchase for a month made me rethink my spending habits.

definition: money you save for unexpected costs, such as losing your job
example: Financial experts suggest building an emergency fund before you start investing.

definition: to pay for something in several smaller amounts over time
example: The store let me pay in instalments, but the total cost was higher.

definition: a warning from a bank about suspicious activity on an account
example: I got a fraud alert by text when someone tried to use my card in another country.

definition: a trick in which criminals send fake messages to steal your personal information
vi: lừa đảo qua tin nhắn/email giả mạo (phishing)
example: The email looked real, but it was a phishing scam asking for my banking password.

definition: to block a bank card temporarily so no one can use it
example: You can freeze a card in the app while you search for it at home.

definition: to exchange a cheque for money at a bank
example: Some banks charge a fee to cash a cheque if you don't have an account with them.
collocations: cash a cheque at the bank

definition: the value of one country's money compared with another's
example: I check the exchange rate before I send money to my parents in Vietnam.

definition: a record of how you have borrowed and repaid money in the past
example: Newcomers often have no Canadian credit history, which makes renting harder.

definition: to create a good record of borrowing and repaying so lenders trust you
vi: xây dựng lịch sử tín dụng (tạo uy tín vay nợ)
example: Using a credit card with a low limit and paying it off every month is a simple way to build credit.

definition: to pay the whole amount at one time
example: You can pay in full today or spread the cost of the sofa over twelve months.
collocations: pay in full by the due date

definition: an amount of money charged once a year, often for a credit card
example: This travel card has great rewards, but the annual fee is quite high.

definition: interest paid on both the original money and the interest already earned
example: Thanks to compound interest, saving a little from a young age really adds up.

definition: to sign a loan with someone and promise to pay if they cannot
vi: đồng ký tên bảo lãnh (cùng ký khoản vay)
example: My uncle agreed to co-sign my car loan because I had no credit history yet.

definition: a home loan whose interest rate does not change for a set period
vi: khoản vay mua nhà lãi suất cố định
example: We chose a fixed-rate mortgage so our payments would stay the same for five years.

definition: the crime of using someone else's personal information to steal money
example: Shred old bank statements to protect yourself from identity theft.

definition: a fast electronic transfer of money between banks, often to another country
vi: chuyển tiền điện tử liên ngân hàng (thường ra nước ngoài)
example: To send money to my sister in Vietnam, I used a wire transfer because e-transfers only work within Canada.

definition: an organization such as a bank or credit union that handles money
example: Contact your financial institution immediately if you notice any unusual activity.

definition: to not pay the full amount owed on a credit card each month
vi: để dư nợ thẻ tín dụng sang tháng sau (không trả hết mỗi tháng)
example: If you carry a balance on your credit card, the interest can add up quickly.
collocations: carry a balance from month to month

definition: to have just enough money to pay for the things you need
vi: xoay xở đủ sống, kiếm đủ để trang trải
example: With rent going up, many families in Metro Vancouver struggle to make ends meet.

definition: to spend all your pay before you receive the next one, with nothing saved
vi: sống tháng nào hết tháng đó (không có tiền dư)
example: Many young workers live paycheque to paycheque and have no savings at all.
collocations: many people live paycheque to paycheque

definition: to have very little money available at the moment
vi: đang kẹt tiền, đang túng tiền
example: I'm a bit strapped for cash this month, so I'll skip the concert.
collocations: strapped for cash after the holidays

definition: told by a lender, before you make a final application, that you can borrow up to a certain amount
example: Get pre-approved for a mortgage before you start going to open houses.

definition: the conditions for paying back a loan, such as how long and how much
example: Read the repayment terms carefully before you sign any loan agreement.

definition: the period of time between two credit card or utility bills
vi: kỳ thanh toán (chu kỳ hoá đơn)
example: Purchases made after the billing cycle ends will appear on next month's statement.

definition: to combine several debts into one loan, often to get a lower interest rate
vi: gộp các khoản nợ thành một
example: She took out a single loan to consolidate debt from three different credit cards.

definition: to fail to make the required payments on a loan
vi: vỡ nợ, không trả được khoản vay
example: If you default on a loan, your credit score can drop sharply.
collocations: risk of defaulting on a loan

definition: to gradually build up interest over time
vi: tích luỹ lãi, lãi phát sinh dần
example: Unpaid credit card balances accrue interest until they are paid off.

definition: to spread your money across different types of investments to reduce risk
example: Our financial advisor told us to diversify instead of putting everything into one stock.

definition: something valuable, such as a house or car, that a lender can take if you do not repay a loan
example: The bank asked for collateral before approving the business loan.

definition: an interest rate that can go up or down over time
vi: lãi suất thả nổi (lãi suất biến đổi)
example: With a variable rate, our mortgage payments went up when interest rates rose.
